what_its_for: Haloperidol is used to treat mental health conditions such as schizophrenia (a condition that affects how you think, feel, and behave) and to control severe behavioral problems. It can also help reduce tics and uncontrolled speech sounds in people with Tourette syndrome. Sometimes doctors use it to treat severe agitation or nausea.
how_to_take: Take haloperidol exactly as your doctor tells you to. You can take the tablet form with or without food. If you are using the liquid concentrate form, carefully measure your dose with the dropper provided and mix it into a small amount of water, juice, or another beverage just before taking it — do not mix it ahead of time. Swallow tablets whole. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it to find the right amount for you. The dose is different for every person depending on your condition, age, weight, and how your body responds. Do not change your dose or stop taking it on your own without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better. Stopping suddenly can cause withdrawal symptoms.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store haloperidol tablets and liquid at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the liquid from freezing. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused medication safely — ask your pharmacist about drug take-back programs in your area.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking haloperidol, as it can increase dizziness, drowsiness, and other side effects. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medication affects you. Avoid getting overheated — stay cool in hot weather and drink plenty of fluids. Avoid standing up too quickly, as this medicine can cause a drop in blood pressure that may make you feel dizzy or faint. Tell all your doctors and dentists that you take this medication before any procedures.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: uncontrolled muscle movements in your face, tongue, or body (such as lip smacking, grimacing, or jerking); stiff or rigid muscles; high fever; fast or irregular heartbeat; confusion or unusual behavior; trouble breathing or swallowing; severe restlessness or an uncontrollable urge to keep moving; seizures; yellowing of your skin or eyes; or signs of a very serious but rare condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) which includes high fever, stiff muscles, confusion, and sweating. Also call your doctor if you feel depressed, have thoughts of self-harm, or notice any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: You may notice some improvement in agitation or behavior within a few days, but it often takes several weeks — sometimes 4 to 6 weeks or longer — to feel the full benefit of haloperidol for conditions like schizophrenia. Keep taking your medication even if you do not notice immediate improvement. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults: Older people may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness, falls, confusion, and movement problems. This medicine is generally used with extra caution in elderly patients, especially those with dementia, as it may increase the risk of serious side effects. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Haloperidol may cause movement problems or withdrawal symptoms in newborns if used during pregnancy. Breastfeeding: This medication passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Haloperidol can be used in children for certain conditions, but the dose will be carefully adjusted by your doctor based on your child's age and weight.
